findings.title: Update invalidation compares an organization-aware model against a raw model
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate receives `original` from getById(), which returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(): its isEnabled() is false whenever the linked organization is disabled, regardless of the IdP's stored enabled flag. `updated` is the raw caller-supplied model whose isEnabled() ignores organization state. The LoginFilter.ENABLED predicate therefore measures different things on the two sides. For example, while an organization is disabled, changing a public org IdP from hideOnLogin=false to hideOnLogin=true yields predicate(original)=false (org disabled) and predicate(updated)=false (hidden), so no invalidation is registered; yet the cached getForLogin ID set was populated from the JPA delegate, which selects on stored fields only and contains this IdP. Once the organization is re-enabled, the stale cached set returns the now-hidden IdP (its per-IdP model is freshly fetched, so it appears enabled), and login-page callers that only re-check isEnabled() will display it. The invalidation decision must be made on comparable, storage-level enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin/brokerPublic values for both models.

findings.title: getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
findings.body: The cached IDs are collected into a Set (Collectors.toSet() at line 229/238) and the result is rebuilt by iterating a new HashSet (line 244) and returning identityProviders.stream(). Unlike the uncached path, which preserves the JPA/delegate stream order, the cached path returns IdPs in hash iteration order. IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin has no documented unordered contract, so callers that do not explicitly sort (the contract previously returned getAllStream order) can see login IdPs in a different, unstable order once the cache is populated versus on the first, uncached call.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes a literal alias instead of the created IdPs
findings.body: Inside the loop creating idp-alias-0..19, the cleanup is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable (alias/idp-alias-i). The cleanup therefore never removes the 20 created identity providers (and likewise the idp-alias-20 cleanup at line 425). Leftover enabled/public IdPs can leak into subsequent tests sharing the realm and skew login-IdP counts, making this and other cache tests order-dependent.
